definition: The fraction of predictions that are correct — the most intuitive metric but misleading on imbalanced classes.
details: The fraction of predictions that are correct — the most intuitive metric but misleading on imbalanced classes.

explainer.lead: Accuracy tells you how often a model’s predictions match the correct answers. It is easy to understand, but a high score can hide poor performance on a rare class.

tiers.eli5: Imagine taking a 10-question quiz: if you get 7 answers right, your accuracy is 7 out of 10. But suppose 9 questions are about dogs and only 1 is about a cat. Answering “dog” every time would still give you 9 out of 10, even though you completely failed on cats.
tiers.practitioner: Use accuracy as a quick summary for classification predictions by dividing the number of correct predictions by the total number evaluated. On imbalanced classes, inspect performance for each class as well; predicting the majority class every time can produce deceptively high accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: For n evaluated examples, Accuracy = (1/n) * sum from i=1 to n of I(y_hat_i = y_i), where I is 1 when the predicted and true labels match and 0 otherwise. Equivalently, it is correct predictions divided by total predictions. Its principal limitation here is that class imbalance can allow strong overall accuracy despite systematically failing a minority class.

explainer.example: A model evaluates 100 emails: 90 are not spam and 10 are spam. If it labels every email “not spam,” it gets 90 correct, so its accuracy is 90/100 = 90%, yet it detects none of the spam.

usedIn.name: Email spam filtering
usedIn.detail: Measures how often predicted spam and non-spam labels are correct.

usedIn.name: Image classification
usedIn.detail: Reports the share of images assigned their correct labels.

usedIn.name: Medical screening
usedIn.detail: Summarizes correct classifications, but can be misleading when positive cases are rare.

explainer.intuition: Accuracy is a scoreboard: count every correct prediction, then see what fraction of all predictions that represents. It treats every example equally, regardless of which class it belongs to.
howItWorks: Collect the model’s predictions and the true labels for the same examples.
Compare each prediction with its true label.
Divide that count by the total number of examples.
explainer.whyItMatters: Accuracy provides a simple way to summarize and compare prediction performance. Knowing its weakness with imbalanced classes helps prevent a reassuring overall score from concealing failures that matter.
misconceptions: High accuracy does not necessarily mean good performance on every class.
Accuracy alone cannot reveal which kinds of mistakes a model makes.
A model that always predicts the majority class can still score highly.

diagram.caption: Accuracy compares predictions with true labels and reports the fraction that match.
